test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The Guptas issued a large number of gold coins called ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dinaras**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Gupta Empire**, which flourished from the **4th to 6th century CE**, is renowned for issuing the **largest number of gold coins** in ancient Indian history. These gold coins were professionally known as **Dinaras**.
 
• The term **Dinara** is believed to have been derived from the **Roman currency** known as **Denarius**, reflecting the strong trade links between India and the Western world during that era.
 
• The **Gupta gold coins** were not only a medium of exchange but also served as a medium for **royal propaganda**, depicting the kings in various poses such as playing the **Veena**, hunting lions, or performing religious sacrifices.
 
• The early **Gupta coinage** was heavily influenced by the **Kushana** style, but later rulers introduced indigenous elements, including **Sanskrit inscriptions** and figures of Indian deities like **Lakshmi** and **Garuda**.
 
• While the Guptas issued the **maximum number** of gold coins, it is noted by historians that the **purity of gold** in these coins gradually declined during the later part of the dynasty compared to the high-purity coins of the **Kushanas**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tanka and Jital:**

 
 
• The **Tanka** (silver coin) and **Jital** (copper coin) were the standard currencies introduced much later by the **Delhi Sultanate**.
 
• **Iltutmish**, the Sultan of the **Slave Dynasty**, is credited with introducing these coins in the **13th century** to stabilize the economy of the Sultanate. ***Hence, options 2 and 3 are incorrect in the context of the Guptas.***
 
 
 
• **Rupakas (Silver Coins):**
 
 
• The Guptas also issued silver coins known as **Rupakas**.
 
• The issuance of silver coins was primarily started by **Chandragupta II** (Vikramaditya) after his successful military campaign and victory over the **Saka Kshatrapas** of Western India.
 
 
 
• **Copper Coins:**
 
 
• While gold and silver were prominent, **copper coins** were also issued by Gupta rulers like **Ramagupta** and **Chandragupta II**, though they are found in much smaller quantities compared to the **Dinaras**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance:**
 
 
• The abundance of **Dinaras** indicates a flourishing **money economy** and significant **long-distance trade**. However, the scarcity of copper coins in later periods suggests a possible decline in local trade or a shift towards **barter systems** for daily transactions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Samudragupta:** Known as the **"Napoleon of India,"** his coins are famous for the **"Lyrist type"** depicting him playing the **Veena**, which highlights his interest in music and art.
 
• **Chandragupta I:** He is often credited with the **"King-Queen type"** coins, which featured him alongside his wife **Kumaradevi**, a princess of the **Lichchhavi** clan.
 
• **Iconography:** The reverse side of the **Gupta gold coins** frequently featured the **Goddess Lakshmi** seated on a lotus, symbolizing prosperity, which became a hallmark of Indian numismatics.
 
• **Decline of Coinage:** Following the **Huna invasions** and the internal disintegration of the empire in the **6th century**, the standard and quantity of the **Dinaras** saw a sharp decline, marking the end of the **Golden Age** of Indian coinage.
